_about: Fields the website needs that Beyond-The-Jersey/data doesn't publish yet (UPDATE.md §9), plus fixes. scripts/build-live-data.ts merges this onto the data repo's normalized/ and writes data/live/. Copy from the design handover is marked 'design'; everything marked 'generated' was written on 2026-09-25 only from the claims it cites, is a draft (status: draft) and needs a review. Send these fields to the data agent so they can move upstream.

clean.plain: We checked every sponsor on the shirt and found nothing.

spotted.plain: A lesser link, like a sponsor that a state partly owns.

stained.plain: A sponsor with a serious record on the front, or a severe one elsewhere on the shirt.

soaked.plain: A sponsor with a severe record on the front, or two serious ones.

why.text: Dubai is part of the United Arab Emirates, where criticising the government can land you in prison. In 2024, 43 activists got life sentences in a single mass trial. Putting Emirates on a famous shirt makes the country look good to millions of fans while that goes on. That’s called sportswashing.
why.messageLine: In 2024, 43 activists in the UAE got life sentences in one mass trial.

why.text: Rwanda’s government pays to put its tourism brand on the shirt. UN experts say 3,000–4,000 Rwandan troops are fighting alongside M23 rebels in eastern Congo, where the rebels take about $800,000 a month from coltan mining. A famous shirt makes Rwanda look like a holiday destination while that goes on. That’s called sportswashing.
why.messageLine: UN experts say 3,000–4,000 Rwandan troops are fighting alongside M23 rebels in eastern Congo.

why.text: Riyadh Air belongs to Saudi Arabia’s state fund, which the crown prince chairs. A famous shirt makes the country look good to millions of fans while that goes on. That’s called sportswashing.
why.messageLine: Saudi Arabia carried out a record 345 executions in 2024.

why.text: Etihad is owned by the Government of Abu Dhabi, part of the United Arab Emirates. Putting Etihad on a famous shirt makes the country look good to millions of fans while that goes on. That’s called sportswashing.
why.messageLine: In 2024, 43 activists in the UAE got life sentences in one mass trial, and the convictions were upheld in 2025.

claimEdits._about: Rating commentary inside claim texts ('State ownership alone earns serious', 'Human-rights relevance is remote') isn't in the sources and contradicts the holds, so it is taken out. Exact text; a claim whose text has changed upstream is reported, not edited.
ut-southwestern-medical-center-record: State ownership of one half of the patch drives a state tier. Human-rights relevance is limited to public-sector healthcare and labour policy.
eni-record: State ownership alone earns serious. Eni's upstream operations in Libya, Egypt, Nigeria and Mozambique give it live, conflict-adjacent human-rights exposure on top.
osceola-county-tourism-authority-record: Because the owner is a public body, the state-owner rule puts it in 'serious'. Human-rights relevance is remote - a local government tourism body with no armed-conflict or conflict-minerals exposure.
friuli-venezia-giulia-region-record: The owner is therefore a public authority - 'serious' under the state-owner rule. Human-rights relevance: a regional government's destination marketing, with no conflict or minerals exposure.
university-of-texas-system-record: State ownership, so 'serious' under the rule. Human-rights relevance: public healthcare/research, no conflict exposure.
sinochem-holdings-record: A Chinese state owner of that size is a material state link on a Ferrari sponsor.
axpo-holding-ag-record: The Genoa front sponsor is therefore backed by sub-national Swiss state capital.
regione-autonoma-della-sardegna-record: It is a public-law regional body, so this is sub-national state money.
